A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Thinkless research work, with readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting reliable comparison. Both end with references on page 12; neither contains appendix pages, despite in-text references to an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original Thinkless benchmark results in Table 1, distillation experiments in Table 2, and training-dynamics and case analyses in Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, distillation, training-dynamics, and case-study results reported in v1.

M1.justification: The distillation procedure, control tokens, reward function, and decoupled optimization objective are unchanged. Section 4.1 corrects the algorithm's expanded name without changing its procedure or equations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OpenR1/OpenThoughts distillation datasets and DeepScaleR reinforcement-learning data, and evaluate on AIME 2024, Minerva Algebra, MATH-500, and GSM8K.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same base models, Merging configurations, CoT-Valve configurations, and Random/Q-7B routers. The vanilla GRPO comparison in Section 4.3 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The model configuration, training budgets, sampling settings, and evaluation metrics remain identical. Both retain one SFT epoch, 600 RL steps, eight sampled responses per query, and the same reported accuracy, token-count, and thinking-frequency metrics.

E4.justification: Both retain the mode-collapse analysis, control-token weight comparison of 0.5 versus 0.001, distillation-dataset comparison, and MATH-500 case study in Sections 4.3–4.5.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the reported benchmark results.

E6.justification: All table entries, plotted results, and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 gives Thinkless the same Minerva Algebra Pass@1 of 0.9459, 1,144 tokens, and 25.88% thinking frequency in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, reward specification, and derivations in Section 3, including Equations 1–4, are identical. No assumptions, proofs, or formal results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive reasoning-mode selection, stabilized training through DeGRPO, and reduced use of long-form reasoning.

C2.justification: The explanations of mode collapse, learning dynamics, and task allocation are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning warm-up performance degradation and restricted RL domain coverage.

D1.justification: Hardware, frameworks, hyperparameters, context lengths, and code-access information are unchanged. Both report four H100 GPUs and the same Megatron/VeRL implementation details; neither supplies the referenced appendix.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research positioning, and all 44 references are unchanged. The corrected GRPO expansion does not introduce a different relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: Section 4.1 changes 'Decoupled Generalized Reweighted Policy Optimization' to 'Decoupled Group Relative Policy Optimization.' The author emails are reordered and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–2 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Page organization is unchanged apart from incidental line wrapping caused by the wording correction.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects a local algorithm-name error and aligns email order with author order. Since v1 already names and formulates DeGRPO correctly in Section 3, these editorial corrections do not meaningfully change the paper's scientific clarity, empirical support, reproducibility, or limitations.
